## Verify Signature (VS)

Input: `contract`. Output: `clean`, `ceremonyState`, `blockingCount`, `findings[]` (one sentence each, prefixed with the signing order), `nextToRequest`, `message`.

Re-fetches the contract (never trusts the caller's load state), then runs `verifyCeremony` from signature-block-field against the Signatory cards **as they are now** — authority ceiling vs contract value, contract type covered, still active, every line named and backed by a legal entity, signing order unique and respected, every signed line carrying a reference. A signatory deactivated after the request went out fails here even though it passed at request time; that is the point of re-deriving rather than caching.

Writes nothing. It is the audit read; Request Signature and Execute Contract call the same function as their guard.

### Example

Natural target: Contract — Acme Industries MSA 2026 (two signed lines; returns clean, ceremony complete).

### Non-goals

No provider callbacks or webhook ingestion. Does not mark anything signed — a line's `status` is set by the provider record (or by hand for wet ink).
